why: a call that never returns would never fail: the hang
a timed-out call would read as an ordinary failure and end the whole page group
a clock step that never returns would hang
the timed-out call would not name the forcing step
a wrapped page would lose its draft errors, so an uncaught draft error would no longer fail the settle
an inline evaluate would not be named
a timed-out visit would end the page group's later visits
the stuck page would be reused for the next visit
a timed-out visit would leave its width decided, so a stuck row could read as a defect
the gap row would not name the route that hung
a hang would not name its visit in the progress file

find: log( `${ v.label } at ${ width }: timed out (${ what })` );
why: a timed-out visit would not be logged
a forcing CDP call that timed out would be swallowed and the visit would go on calling a stuck page
a stuck clock step would become a draft-timer error and lose its timed-out mark
a wrapped page would lose its draft errors
